question: Does ordinary gameplay reach the static defeat NULL animation-node writes?
checkpoint_origin: Verified ordinary-joystick reverse-security-damage route; no guest-state edits for this probe. Local snapshot is intentionally not published.
interpretation: First original damage store reached and HP changed from 95 to 44.
Second damage store did not occur within the bounded 12-second phase; later phases did not execute. This does not establish unreachability.
At both captured first-hit stops, bytes 0x8..0x13 were 00fc081800fc081a00fc081c.

Isolated original CPU regression establishes that a NULL node clears bit 0 of byte 0xA and the word at 0x10. Byte 0xA belongs to the bus-error vector; word 0x10 is the high word of the illegal-instruction vector.

The observed byte 0xA is 0x08, whose bit 0 is already clear. The word at 0x10 is 0x00fc; a later NULL-node call would zero that word if unchanged. This conditional effect was not observed in gameplay.
No corrected variant or patch record was implemented because ordinary gameplay reachability remains unconfirmed.
next_step: Use bounded ordinary joystick movement to remain near or follow the responding actor, or establish an independently reproducible normal defeat route; do not force HP or pointers.

startup_diagnosis.cause: unknown; emulator output is discarded by the launcher, temporary endpoint directory is cleaned, and the failed CLI log was overwritten by the subsequent run
startup_diagnosis.comparison: Earlier first-damage invocation and later death-path invocation used the same executable, legal ROM and deterministic direct-payload contract. First-damage succeeded; later permission-added invocation completed with an incomplete gameplay scenario. This does not isolate a permissions cause.

permission_request.reason_for_request: Inference from restricted sandbox and loopback debugger use, not a demonstrated socket failure. No further escalation is justified by the startup exit alone.

startup_diagnosis.separate_restoration_api_error: A subsequent ordinary restoration state request failed with urlopen error [Errno 1] Operation not permitted; this establishes a restriction on that connection, not the cause of the earlier emulator exit.

next_damage_preconditions: Player active; no combat gate while flash is zero.
Existing flash advances for 31 service calls without decrementing damage countdown.
After flash, a non-NULL nearby object must resolve to a position state with flag bit 7.
Player must still map to a restricted zone and selected card must fail clearance.
Damage occurs only after the countdown reaches zero from 50 eligible decrements; elapsed wall time alone is insufficient.

tests.scope: Prior eleven policy cases, seven new eligibility/pause/lost-checkpoint cases and four descriptor-partition cases.
Additional original death-branch continuation through actual message and health-draw callees to exchange return.

offline_followup.eligible_counter_progression: With player active, combat off, stable bit7 nearby state, restricted original map cell and insufficient selected clearance: 31 flash service calls leave countdown50 untouched; 49 eligible calls reduce it to1; the next call reaches source887C with D0 low byte0 from HP44, before storing health.
offline_followup.pause_and_resume: Inactive, combat, sufficient card and unrestricted zone each preserve countdown50 and response-active1 for three calls; removing the gate makes the next original service call decrement to49.
offline_followup.lost_checkpoint: NULL nearest pointer and non-bit7 state each branch to source8848 before decrement. The audio-clearing helper is not executed in these bounded cases.

assumptions: Already-busy status queue with tail at its empty head; initialized original player descriptor and NULL-node static defeat state.
Original compact-font bitmap pointer supplied. Low-memory sentinel byteA=A5 and word10=BEEF explicitly supplied.
No forced register restoration after message/health callees; no replaced instructions or stubbed callbacks.
observed: Original outcome/rank calls append three messages and retain A4 context until the caller stages static defeat.
Actual health draw completes; exchange binds static defeat state and saves previous state.
A5 remains the player, byteA becomesA4 and word10 becomes0.
death_continuation.trace_bound: At most4096 instructions, collected in64-instruction chunks preserving all CPU/stack state; each chunk must complete without trace-range overflow or error diagnostics.
death_continuation.limit: Starting at the death branch is synthetic local execution. It does not demonstrate that ordinary joystick play reaches the branch.

offline_followup.conclusion: The caller/callee continuity gap is closed for this explicit local state. Ordinary-input reachability is still unresolved; optional corrected build remains deferred.
